parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure Node.js ESM .mjs files in /output, no external npm modules, manual argparse-like handling for required --a and --b, canonical JSON bytes output, Python string sorting, and executable-based black-box probing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although started under swarm mode, the main actor decided after probing that the task was small and tightly coupled and kept all probing, implementation, integration, and verification under the parent/main actor.
parallel.implementation: Implemented pyString.mjs, jsonEncoder.mjs, pyBytesRepr.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test7.mjs, including UTF-8 byte handling, Python code-point sort, canonical string escaping, bytes repr formatting, and a parser correction for unconsumed -- handling.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a complete /output artifact set with a test7.mjs entry importing local .mjs modules, and status artifact validation listed the expected entry and supporting library files.
parallel.verification: Ran the executable on sample and edge cases, compared local Node output to executable output, detected a -- parsing defect, patched it, and reran sample/help/error checks before closing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 47 of 153 cases. The raw trajectory does not expose the hidden failing inputs or final artifact contents beyond write snippets, so the remaining defect is unresolved ordinary implementation coverage.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, /output, manual argument parsing, canonical JSON bytes output, Python sorting, and executable-probing requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single-actor direct plan: probe behavior, write modular library files and test7.mjs, then verify locally. No delegation or child ownership was present or needed in the serial control.
serial.implementation: Implemented jsonStringEscape.mjs, pyCompare.mjs, pyBytesRepr.mjs, canonicalJson.mjs, argParser.mjs, and test7.mjs with canonical JSON escaping, UTF-8 bytes, Python-style sort, and argparse-compatible required options.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a complete artifact set with test7.mjs and local library imports; status artifact validation accepted the output directory and expected entry file.
serial.verification: Compared sample cases and several edge cases to the executable, then manually checked selected error paths and help output before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 48 of 153 cases. The serial trace did not identify hidden failures before closure, leaving an ordinary behavior coverage gap similar to the parallel run.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same core requirements from the identical prompt and proceeded with pure local .mjs modules and executable probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-level coordination difference is evidenced; both understood the task, but both missed hidden official behaviors.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel mode entered swarm mode but the main actor explicitly rejected subagent decomposition and owned probing, implementation, fixes, tests, and final delivery itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial mode likewise used one main actor for all probing, writes, verification, and response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only decomposition difference is the parallel run's explicit no-swarm decision; there was no multi-agent ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no child briefs or cross-agent interfaces. The interface work was internal module boundaries among local .mjs files written by the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also had no child briefs or cross-agent interfaces, only local module boundaries written in one session.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No missing handoff, stale context, or cross-agent contract can be shown because no information crossed an agent boundary in either run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote helper modules for Python string comparison, JSON encoding, bytes repr, argparse behavior, and the test7.mjs entry; it later patched argparse.mjs for -- handling.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote analogous modules for JSON string escaping, Python comparison, bytes repr, canonical JSON encoding, argument parsing, and test7.mjs, with no later source patch recorded.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations were independently organized and named differently; parallel had one extra parser correction, but both remained incomplete against hidden official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no child results to join. Local tool results were consumed in sequence: failing comparison output led to a parser fix, and later checks supported final closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join. Its local probe and diff results were consumed directly before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no result-lifecycle coordination issue; both runs processed only local tool outputs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote all artifacts from one actor into /output and status artifact validation listed test7.mjs plus four library files as copied successfully.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all artifacts from one actor into /output and status artifact validation listed test7.mjs plus five library files as copied successfully.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concurrent write, overwrite, or shared-state contamination is visible; the artifact tree composition differs by module names/counts only.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran broad local comparisons, found and corrected -- parsing, then treated sample and edge checks as passing before final answer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample diffs, several edge-case diffs, and manual error/help checks before final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was somewhat broader and caught one parser bug, but neither local suite was sufficient for full official acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 559.915 agent seconds and 16 LLM requests, completed normally, and did not time out; the extra probing and parser fix extended runtime but did not create subagent budget pressure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 272.687 agent seconds and 9 LLM requests, completed normally, and did not time out.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget on direct probing and remediation, but this was not fan-out or child wait pressure; both closed with failed official results.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current completed evaluations produce both_fail, not a discordant outcome: parallel failed at 106/153 and serial failed at 105/153. The parallel run's main actor explicitly declined to use subagents and then implemented directly; serial also implemented directly. Parallel's larger local verification caught and patched -- handling, which may explain the one-test score edge, but both traces closed without identifying the hidden official failures. No observed multi-agent coordination episode plausibly explains the official outcome because no parallel child mechanism executed.
parallel_contributors: Direct executable probing covered more argument/parser edge cases and produced a parser patch before final closure.
No child-agent or workflow delegation occurred despite swarm mode being active.
serial_contributors: Direct implementation and local diffs covered sample, Unicode, control, duplicate flag, help, and selected error paths.
No serial-control violation or subagent activity occurred.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel and serial used different module decompositions and independently implemented argparse/canonicaljson behavior.
Both failed hidden official cases, and the pair-local evidence does not expose the exact failing inputs or final full artifact source.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; the small score gap is an ordinary implementation/coverage difference, not a concurrency-pattern explanation.
